LESSON: WEATHER AND THE SKY

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade one
Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES
Strand: Natural environment
Topic 2.1: Weather and the sky
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 12

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Weather and the sky, part of Natural environment in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade one ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: How is the weather today? 2. Why do we study weather?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. describe the appearance of the sky during the day and at night,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Weather and the sky in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Weather and the sky in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Weather and the sky in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. appreciate differences in weather conditions at different times of the day. ● Learners with low vision use digital devices with assistive technology to watch a video while learners with blindness listen to audio clips about the sky during the day and at night and share their findings on the appearances. ● In groups, learners discuss the differences in the appearance of the sky during the day and at night and record their findings. ● Learners with low vision observe pictures of different weather conditions to manipulate (cloudy, sunny, windy, rainy, calm). SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Weather and the sky together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Communication: learner speaks engagingly when telling age appropriate stories about weather and weather conditions.

Values:
Responsibility: learner enhances resilience as they engage in making and maintaining a daily journal on weather conditions.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills: A Learner learns to manage time as they make and read weather charts.

Link to other Learning Areas:

Appearance of the sky and conditions can be used when learning creation in Religious Activities.

Suggested Learning Resources

Sky (immediate environment), approved support learning materials, digital devices with assistive technology, manilla papers, crayons, pencils,

cotton wool, adhesive glue.
